description: This study updates the landslide inventory along the Karakoram Highway in northern Pakistan, which landslides frequently disrupt. Using a documented inventory, optical imagery and frequency-area statistics, the authors explore slope failures and their controls, then apply persistent scatterer InSAR to Sentinel-1 data from January 2018 to January 2022, measuring slope deformation rates from 0 to 364 mm per year. They classified 234 landslides from the literature, detected 29 new potential landslides, redefined several existing ones and built an updated susceptibility model with 86.6 percent precision by area under the curve, and studied fast-moving sites such as Budalas and Khanabad (over 50 mm per year). Coverage: the highway corridor in Gilgit-Baltistan. Format and access: open access article in Scientific Reports (2023) on PubMed Central. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: no separate data deposit is listed in the article record read. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of mountain highways. It relates to the European Ground Motion Service and the Costa Viola landslide case in the catalogue.
